history.summary: The Madana Gopala Swamy Temple at Jatprole (Jetprole/Jataprolu) is a Krishna temple on the banks of the Srisailam Dam reservoir (Krishna river). Uniquely Telangana records it was built in the 12th century by Malla Naidu, son of Recherla Bethi Reddy, and in the 16th century the samsthan passed to the Surbhi Rajas under the Vijayanagara king. During construction of the Srisailam Dam it was relocated (1989) from its original site at Manchalakatta/Malleswaram on the left bank of the Krishna to the present site near Jatprole. The temple has a tall rajagopuram, large wooden gates, a spacious sabhamandapa whose pillars are carved in Vijayanagara style, entrances on four sides, several sub-shrines and a group of shivalayas nearby. BUILD-DATE CONFLICT (flag): Uniquely Telangana says 12th century (Malla Naidu); Omastrology says originally built in the 16th century AD - verify.
